title: The Kindly Visitor
premise: Oscar Brightwater returns to the drowning village of Hollowmere to bury her twin sister Odile, only to find the death certificate names Oscar herself. When the church bell — melted down in 1911 — rings across the marsh, Oscar learns that in 1974 her grandmother took something from the thing that lives beneath the mere: a child, swapped for a blessing. The village's long prosperity was bought with that theft, and every generation has paid interest. As the harvest moon rises, Oscar must uncover what was taken, return it to the water, and choose between the twin who died and the truth of which one actually survived.
about_author: Isandro Kavanagh is the pen name of a former parish archivist from the East Anglian fens who spent a decade cataloguing drowned villages before turning to fiction. Their work blends folk horror with quiet domestic grief, and they claim never to write after dark.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Oscar arrives in Hollowmere by bus through fog, carrying her sister's ashes and a funeral program with her own name printed on it. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: disoriented grief sharpening into unease as villagers greet her with pity meant for someone else.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Settling into the family house, Oscar catalogs the noises she has spent a decade rationalizing — footsteps above, her name called in Odile's voice. A letter from her grandmother Edith, dated 1974, surfaces under floorboards. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: dread replacing denial.

chapters.title: A Church Without a Bell
chapters.summary: At the funeral, the vicar refuses to hold the service at dusk. Old Mr. Tallow mentions the bell was melted for scrap in 1911, yet everyone flinches when it tolls once, distantly, over the mere. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: communal fear she cannot yet name.

chapters.title: What Edith Kept
chapters.summary: Reading Edith's letter, Oscar learns of a bargain struck in 1974: something taken from the water, something given in return. The letter names a date — the harvest moon — and begs forgiveness. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: inherited guilt arriving like a debt notice.

chapters.title: The Mere at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Oscar walks the drained margins of the mere and finds a stone marker reading 'RETURNED 1911' beside fresh wet footprints leading away from the water. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the first hard evidence that the village's folklore is inventory, not invention.

chapters.title: Tallow's Confession
chapters.summary: The ancient verger, half-drunk on memorial sherry, tells her about the Kindly Visitor — the thing in the mere that grants wishes politely and collects them slowly. He was a boy in 1974; he saw what Edith carried home wrapped in a coat. POV: Oscar with Tallow's recounted memory. Emotional beat: horrified fascination.

chapters.title: Odile's Room
chapters.summary: Searching her twin's locked room, Oscar finds diaries in which Odile recorded hearing their grandmother's voice for years — and a final entry: 'It isn't asking anymore.' POV: Oscar reading Odile. Emotional beat: grief curdling into the suspicion that Odile's death was not natural.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers Wrongly
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews neighbors whose memories of 1974 contradict each other and the parish records; photographs show an extra child in every group shot, always blurred. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: loneliness of being the only one keeping accurate books.

chapters.title: Bargain Economics
chapters.summary: Tallow explains the arrangement: the Visitor protects Hollowmere's harvests and heals its sick, but the stolen child must be returned or a replacement accepted. Every family has quietly decided it won't be theirs. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: moral nausea at how ordinary complicity looks.

chapters.title: The Second Bell
chapters.summary: The melted bell rings nine times at midnight; in the morning, nine villagers remember nothing of the past year. The Visitor is shortening its patience. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: escalating stakes made audible.

chapters.title: Edith's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the bank vault, Oscar finds Edith's ledger listing payments made across fifty years — small kindnesses, then livestock, then names. The final page is blank except for tomorrow's date and two entries: O. BRIGHTWATER, twice. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold clarity about the trap.

chapters.title: Which Twin
chapters.summary: A dream sequence in the flooded church: Odile appears and insists Oscar is the one who died in 2015, that Oscar has been the noise in the house all along. POV: Oscar/Odile, unstable. Emotional beat: identity vertigo — the reader can no longer be sure.

chapters.title: The Coat in the Wall
chapters.summary: Following Tallow's memory, Oscar opens a bricked alcove and finds the 1974 coat, inside it a child's shoe and a locket engraved with a name no villager will say aloud: Merrin Vane. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: tenderness toward the victim breaking through fear.

chapters.title: Merrin
chapters.summary: Parish records reveal Merrin Vane, age seven, drowned in 1974 — or was taken. Her mother lived another thirty years leaving offerings at the mere every full moon. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Committee of Silence
chapters.summary: The village council confronts Oscar: returning Merrin ends the protection; they offer her Odile's place instead — stay, be remembered, let the ledger close. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: temptation offered in the language of belonging.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Oscar burns the ledger pages bearing living names and announces at the pub that the bargain ends at the harvest moon. That night every door in the village turns to face the water. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: defiant isolation, the cost named aloud.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Preparing for the return, Oscar learns from Tallow that giving back requires a keeper — someone must walk Merrin to the middle and stay until the moon sets. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: acceptance of personal sacrifice without melodrama.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: The moon rises fat and low. The mere stands perfectly still. The Visitor comes up the lane as a tall courteous figure wearing Edith's face, and asks, kindly, whether Oscar has brought what was taken. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: terror rendered as terrible politeness.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: Oscar carries Merrin's remains into the black water, reciting the names Edith's ledger stole. The Visitor counts them, finds the account balanced, and reaches for Oscar anyway — until Odile's voice, real at last, answers the counting. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: climax where loyalty literally intercedes.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Stone
chapters.summary: The Visitor accepts Odile — the twin who had already been listening for ten years — as the closing payment, and the bell rings once, whole and bronze, then falls silent forever. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: devastating relief braided with loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the village remembers everything now, and hates Oscar for it. She restores Merrin Vane's grave, gives Tallow the truth he'd carried since boyhood, and packs the house. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: bitter peace; truth costs community.

chapters.title: The Kindly Visitor
chapters.summary: Leaving Hollowmere, Oscar passes the mere one last time. Far out, something raises a hand in polite farewell — and she hears, unmistakably, both her own voice and Odile's say goodbye. She does not look back twice. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: haunted closure; inheritance survived, memory kept, loyalty honored.
